::: {.hero-lede}
# Rodents, land use and the risk of spillover

I study how people reshape landscapes, how small mammals respond, and where
that leaves the viruses they carry. Most of this work is on Lassa fever in
West Africa.
:::

:::

```{=html}
<ul class="gradient-key">
  <li style="--band: var(--hab-forest)">
    <strong>Closed forest</strong>
    <span>Forest specialists, rarely in contact with people. Where sampling effort is thinnest.</span>
  </li>
  <li style="--band: var(--hab-farm)">
    <strong>Farm bush</strong>
    <span>Regrowth and cultivation. The species mix turns over fastest here.</span>
  </li>
  <li style="--band: var(--hab-village)">
    <strong>Village periphery</strong>
    <span>Where <em>Mastomys natalensis</em> peaks, and where most spillover is thought to happen.</span>
  </li>
  <li style="--band: var(--hab-dwelling)">
    <strong>Dwelling</strong>
    <span>Commensal rodents, where invasive species can displace the reservoir.</span>
  </li>
</ul>
```
